message.content: We need a database for the booking app. Postgres or SQLite? We are a team of two.

content.text: For two people and one server, SQLite is simplest. Postgres is the safer choice if you expect several app servers or heavy concurrent writes. A third option is a hosted database such as Firebase, which removes the ops work but ties you to one vendor.

message.content: Go with Postgres. We will have a worker process writing at the same time as the web app.

content.text: Postgres it is. I'll set up a local container and a migration tool.

message.content: Skip Firebase, I do not want vendor lock-in.

content.text: Understood, Firebase is off the table. Two things I have not decided for you: a cache layer such as Redis, and multi-region failover. I would hold off on both until there is real traffic.

message.content: Agreed, hold off on multi-region. We can revisit when we have customers outside the US.

content.text: Parked: multi-region failover. Next, authentication. Options are email links, passwords, or a social login.

message.content: Email magic links only. Passwords are a support burden.

content.text: Magic links. That needs an email provider; I have not picked one.

message.content: Which email provider is cheapest for 5,000 emails a month?

content.text: Prices change, so I would check current pricing before choosing. I have not compared them yet.

message.content: Build the booking table first, then the availability check.

content.text: (a subagent's private reasoning, not part of the conversation)
Booking table and migration are done and the tests pass. The availability check is next.

message.content: The availability check is returning double bookings under load. Fix it with a database constraint, not application code.

content.text: A database-level exclusion constraint fixed the double bookings in the concurrency test. I tried a row lock in application code first; it still allowed a race, so I dropped it.

content.text: Email reminders can reuse the magic-link provider once chosen. Text messages need a separate provider and carrier registration, which takes weeks.

message.content: Email only for now. Texts later maybe.
